about: Guided tour steps. Each step: site (id in data/sites.json), title, text, date (slider position, YYYY-MM-DD), optional change (a change id to open) and note (shown on the timeline). Steps whose site is not ready are skipped. Steps on a fake site (fixture: true) are stand-ins: they run only while no real site in this list is ready.

steps.title: Finland: forest cleared before the check was done
steps.text: Between March and August 2026, about 330 hectares of forest were cleared here at Muhos for a planned Google datacenter, before the required environmental assessment was finished. Radar sees through clouds and at night, even under snow, so the clearing shows up pass after pass.
steps.note: Clearing ran from March to August 2026

steps.title: The stop order came months later
steps.text: The permit authority ordered the work stopped on 6 October 2026, and police opened a preliminary investigation on 29 October. By then the forest was gone. This app is built to flag a change like this while it is still happening, so a person can check it in time.

steps.title: Catalonia: earth moved on a large scale
steps.text: At Agroparc Penedès, a 258-hectare project is moving over 700,000 cubic meters of earth. A court partly halted the works in July 2025 because of protected eagles in the area, and the works have continued since. A change this big is exactly what a planner wants to check against its permits.
steps.note: July 2025: court partly halts the works

steps.title: All of Catalonia at a glance
steps.text: Each colored shape is a change the radar found. Blue looks expected, yellow needs review and orange is a high concern. Press play to watch the changes pile up over the years, then click any shape to see why it got its color.

steps.title: A practice site with fake data
steps.text: The real sites are still being prepared, so this tour runs on a made-up site. Each colored shape is a change the radar found, colored by how urgently a person should look at it.

steps.title: Watch the changes pile up
steps.text: The timeline is back at early 2024. Press play to move forward: each shape appears on the date the radar first saw it, and the background switches to the aerial photo of that year, so you can see the land itself change.
steps.note: Press play to move forward in time

steps.title: A change that needs a look first
steps.text: Forest was cut here in August 2026. The card shows why it is a high concern, with each reason and its source, the pictures from before and after, and the radar signal over time.

steps.title: Not every change is a problem
steps.text: To the radar, this burned area looks like cut forest. It is marked Expected because it matches a recorded wildfire. The app always shows its reasons, so a person can judge for themselves.
